newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE EUROYEN FIRMS AFTER CONFIRMING BOTTOM.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE EUROYEN FIRMS AFTER CONFIRMING BOTTOM.

text.p: Key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures firmed by midday on Thursday after confirming a solid bottom on Wednesday.
Healthy gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures and a retreat in Tokyo stocks this morning were also supportive.

The March contract stopped falling at 99.15 on Wednesday and traders said this prompted a fall in short-term interest rate swap (IRS) rates and provided a reason for bears to buy back the March contract ahead of Japan's machinery order data due out on Friday.
The March stood at 99.20, up 0.05 from Wednesday.
"The contract is hovering around the middle of the recent price range of between 99.15 and 99.22," said a trader at a long-term credit bank.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted a neutral money market operation this morning for the first time since July 17. Traders said the market had expected such an operation.
The key overnight call rate was traded at around 0.47 percent, down from Wednesday's weighted average of 0.48.
The benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.61 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
